text:
amy: Customer (acme-inc) reports a toolcall failing with 400 when sending a Windows path in tool args. Repro from customer:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"pdf_extractor","args":"{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\acme\\invoices\\Q1.pdf\"}"}'
```

They get 400, body: {"error":"tool_args_parse_error","message":"Invalid control character in string at position 62"} Request ID: req_01HXYZ

kevin: Can you paste the exact response headers / request id and any server log snippet?

amy: Response header x-request-id: req_01HXYZ, response body above. From server logs:

JSONParseException: Invalid escape sequence at index 61
  at com.redwood.json.Parser.parseString(Parser.java:123)
  request_id=req_01HXYZ

dave: This looks like unescaped backslashes inside a JSON-encoded string. Quick guidance:
- Best: send args as a JSON object instead of embedding a JSON string. Example:
```json
{"tool":"pdf_extractor","args":{"path":"C:\\Users\\acme\\invoices\\Q1.pdf"}}
```
(When using a shell, prefer single-quoting the outer payload to avoid extra escaping.)

- If you must keep args as a string, you need to escape interior quotes and backslashes. Example value for the `args` field: `"{\"path\":\"C:\\\\Users\\\\acme\\\\invoices\\\\Q1.pdf\"}"` (when placed inside a JSON string).

- Workarounds: have the client use forward slashes in the path (C:/Users/...) or url-encode the path.

Also note: the customer's mobile SDK appears to be double-stringifying and not escaping Windows backslashes when building the request payload. Can devex please triage?

kevin: I'll file a small SDK bug + an infra ticket to add a clearer 400 for this pattern (INF-2345). Will also add a server-side lint that detects likely Windows path patterns with single backslashes and returns: "Invalid escape in tool args string: unescaped backslash\nSee docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/tool-args". :thumbsup:

amy: I'll send the customer the "args as object" example and the escaped-string workaround. Marking customer forwarded; leaving INF-2345 open.

dave: I'll add a short guard in the parsing layer to detect these cases and return the clearer error before the parser throws a low-level exception.
